May take with food to reduce GI upset; separate from antacids/cations by 2 hours
Contraindicated - fluoroquinolones avoided in pregnancy (cartilage toxicity)
Contraindicated - excreted in breast milk; avoid
No major adjustment (hepatic metabolism), but reduce frequency in severe impairment
Reduce dose/frequency in hepatic impairment (extensive hepatic metabolism)
Avoid excess; may worsen CNS effects
Tendon pain, CNS effects, QT/ECG in at-risk patients, blood glucose
summary: Pefloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibacterial active mainly against gram-negative organisms and some gram-positive bacteria, used for susceptible serious infections (urinary, respiratory, skin/soft-tissue, bone/joint, gonorrhea, and some systemic infections) where other agents are unsuitable. It inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. As a fluoroquinolone it shares the class's serious safety profile: tendinitis and tendon rupture, QT prolongation, CNS effects (including seizures), peripheral neuropathy, photosensitivity (notably with pefloxacin), and aortic aneurysm risk - so it is reserved for situations where other antibacterials cannot be used. It is contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, children/adolescents, and in those with quinolone hypersensitivity or tendon disorders. Pefloxacin is NOT approved by the US FDA; this record is based on EMA/national fluoroquinolone product information and class labeling.
indications: Susceptible serious gram-negative infections where other antibacterials are unsuitable
Respiratory tract infections due to susceptible organisms
Uncomplicated gonorrhea (single-dose regimen, where still effective)

dosage.n: IV infusion over ~1 hour; per EMA/national product information

dosage.d: 400 mg twice daily or 800 mg as a single dose (per local guidance)

dosage.n: Only where local quinolone susceptibility remains - widespread resistance limits use

admin: May be taken with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset
Separate from antacids, sucralfate, and iron/zinc/magnesium/calcium products by at least 2 hours (chelation reduces absorption)
Give IV doses by slow infusion (about 1 hour)
Advise avoidance of sun/UV exposure - pefloxacin is notably phototoxic
Reserve for infections where other antibacterials are unsuitable; not FDA-approved (follow EMA/national information)
moa: Pefloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that inhibits the bacterial type II topoisomerases - DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV - which are essential for DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination. Inhibiting these enzymes prevents supercoiling and relaxation of bacterial DNA, leading to bactericidal disruption of DNA synthesis. It is largely metabolized in the liver, with norfloxacin as an active metabolite.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to pefloxacin or other quinolones
Children and growing adolescents (risk of arthropathy/cartilage damage)
History of tendon disorders related to quinolone use
relative: Known QT prolongation, uncorrected electrolyte disturbance, or drugs that prolong QT
Epilepsy or conditions predisposing to seizures
Aortic aneurysm or risk factors for aortic dissection

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Fluoroquinolones are avoided because of the risk of cartilage damage in the developing fetus.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding; pefloxacin is excreted in breast milk and may harm the infant's developing joints.
renal: Pefloxacin is eliminated mainly by hepatic metabolism, so renal impairment has limited effect; dose-frequency reduction may still be considered in severe renal impairment per product information.
hepatic: Because pefloxacin is extensively metabolized by the liver, reduce the dose or dosing frequency in hepatic impairment and monitor for accumulation.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, macrolides, antipsychotics, tricyclics) - additive QT prolongation and arrhythmia risk
Theophylline - pefloxacin raises theophylline levels and seizure risk; monitor levels
moderate: Antacids, sucralfate, and di/trivalent cations (iron, zinc, calcium, magnesium, aluminium) - chelation markedly reduces absorption; separate by >=2 hours
Warfarin / vitamin K antagonists - enhanced anticoagulant effect; monitor INR
Corticosteroids - increased risk of tendon rupture
Antidiabetic agents - dysglycemia (both hypo- and hyperglycemia)
interactions.food: May be taken with food; avoid taking with dairy or cation-containing products at the same time.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol, which may add to CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive opiate screening; can alter glucose readings via dysglycemia.

monitoring: Tendon pain or swelling (stop the drug and rest the limb if suspected)
CNS symptoms (seizures, confusion, neuropathy, mood change)
counsel: Stop the medicine and call your doctor at once if you get tendon pain or swelling, especially at the back of the ankle
Avoid sun and sunlamps and use sun protection - this medicine can cause severe sunburn-like reactions
Do not take it within 2 hours of antacids, iron, calcium, or dairy products
Report any unusual nerve symptoms (numbness, tingling, burning), palpitations, mood changes, or seizures
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a history of tendon problems or heart-rhythm issues
pk: Bactericidal activity begins soon after absorption
Plasma peak about 1.5-2 hours after an oral dose; near-complete oral bioavailability
Store below 25-30 C; protect from light per product information
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this record reflects EMA/national fluoroquinolone product information and class labeling
Class warnings apply: tendinitis/tendon rupture, QT prolongation, CNS/peripheral-neuropathy effects, and aortic aneurysm/dissection - reserve for when other agents cannot be used
Pefloxacin causes notably more photosensitivity than other quinolones - counsel strict sun protection
Contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children/growing adolescents (cartilage toxicity)
Separate from antacids, iron, calcium, and other di/trivalent cations by at least 2 hours to preserve absorption
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up. Complete the full prescribed course.
overdose: Overdose may cause CNS effects (including seizures) and QT prolongation. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive and symptomatic care, ECG monitoring, seizure control, and adequate hydration. Hemodialysis removes little pefloxacin because of high tissue distribution.
